taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-15, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1132.2 | 7.42 | 7.42
2 | 3621.5 | 17.67 | 25.09
3 | 4447.9 | 1.70 | 26.79
4 | 4307.5 | 0.53 | 27.32
5 | 7664.9 | 4.92 | 32.24
6 | 12762.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AKHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-15, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Report: Station T-15 (Survey Area T)**

Station T-15 exhibits a 6-layer geoelectric profile across the surveyed depth:
- Layer 1 (0–7.42 m): 1132.2 Ω·m
- Layer 2 (7.42–25.09 m): 3621.5 Ω·m
- Layer 3 (25.09–26.79 m): 4447.9 Ω·m
- Layer 4 (26.79–27.32 m): 4307.5 Ω·m
- Layer 5 (27.32–32.24 m): 7664.9 Ω·m
- Layer 6 (>32.24 m): 12762.9 Ω·m

Analyzing resistivity trends across consecutive three-layer triplets:
1. Layers 1-2-3 (1132.2 < 3621.5 < 4447.9) → **A**
2. Layers 2-3-4 (3621.5 < 4447.9 > 4307.5) → **K**
3. Layers 3-4-5 (4447.9 > 4307.5 < 7664.9) → **H**
4. Layers 4-5-6 (4307.5 < 7664.9 < 12762.9) → **A**

The calculated sequence matches the on-file AKHA classification. Drilling operations should anticipate high-resistivity bedrock beneath ~27.3 m.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKHA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
